title: Tidewater Logistics - Procurement / MSA & DPA Review
summary: Procurement call to review Redwood MSA/DPA, discuss SLA requirements and pricing approvals for a pilot. Customer requests SOC 2 and data residency clauses, stronger SLAs for latency and uptime for dedicated deployment. Action items include sending redlined MSA, security pack, and pilot scope + pricing sheet.
topics: Pricing for 3-month pilot and committed Dedicated capacity
action_items: Owner: Maya Chen | Item: Send redlined MSA template and DPA with examples of data retention clauses | Due: 2026-04-27
Owner: Ravi Patel | Item: Share pilot runbook and benchmark plan (throughput/latency tests) | Due: 2026-04-29
Owner: Jordan Lee | Item: Provide onboarding timeline and contact for onboarding call | Due: 2026-04-26
next_steps: Redwood to email redlined MSA + DPA and security pack (SOC2 report, architecture diagram)
Customer to review and provide high-level redlines by EOD 2026-04-30
Schedule technical kick-off for pilot w/ SEs and customer infra team week of 2026-05-04
Pricing approval: send 3-month pilot pricing + Dedicated commit options
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (AE): Hey everyone, can you hear me? Good morning, good afternoon. Thanks for joining. We're here to walk through the MSA and DPA and align on SLAs and pilot pricing.
[00:18] Sofia Alvarez (Procurement): Hi Maya, yes, we can hear you. Thanks. Devon, Liam, Maya S are on our side, and we also have a few folks on mute.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Great, quick intros — I'll run through the agenda, Ravi will cover technical SLA questions, and Jordan will handle onboarding and timeline.
[00:42] Ravi Patel (SE): Hi all, quick wave. I'll jump in on the dedicated deployment options and latency guarantees.
[00:50] Liam O'Connor (Head of Security): Hey everyone. Our main ask up front is we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and clarity on key management, like customer-managed KMS or HSM options.
[01:05] Devon Price (Legal): Also, a couple of DPA questions — data residency, subprocessors list, and the right to audit.
[01:18] Maya Chen: Totally, Devon — we'll share our current SOC 2 attestation and a subprocessor list. On KMS, we support customer-managed keys with our private deployment; for hosted we have envelope encryption, and we can discuss HSM integrations.
[01:35] Maya Singh (AI Platform): Quick question on model telemetry: does Redwood retain prompts or logs by default? We need to lock down retention to 30 days for pilot.
[01:45] Jordan Lee (CSM): By default hosted logs are retained 90 days, but on Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and we can set the pilot to 30 days. We'll include that in the DPA examples.
[02:02] Sofia: For SLAs, we can't accept only a best-effort latency — we need p99 under 250ms for common generation path. Is that achievable with Dedicated?
[02:15] Ravi: So, 250ms p99 depends on model and sequence length; for standard 2k token sequences on a quantized model we can hit p99 ~200-300ms on Dedicated with pinned capacity. For hosted it can be more variable. We recommend Dedicated with autoscale and burst capacity for your use case.
[02:40] Devon: On uptime, our procurement wants 99.95% SLA and credits. We saw Redwood's public SLA is 99.9% — any flexibility?
[02:52] Maya Chen: We can offer 99.95% as a contractual SLA for Dedicated customers with a commit level. There are tiers; we'll pull the specific credit table and include it in the redlines.
[03:05] Liam: For the right-to-audit clause, we need reasonable language; we can't do on-site audits but will accept third-party certifications and remote evidence.
[03:18] Maya Chen: Understood. Our standard is to provide SOC 2 and penetration test summaries; for additional asks we can discuss limited remote evidence.
[03:30] [00:03:30] Ravi: On private deployment — if you go VPC-private, you can bring your KMS and network policies. That removes a lot of risk areas for compliance. But it adds onboarding time and ops overhead.
[03:48] Sofia: What's the expected onboarding timeline for Private vs Dedicated? We have a hard window — procurement wants pilot to start by May 10.
[04:00] Jordan: For Dedicated, with committed capacity, onboarding typically takes 2-3 weeks from contract signature. Private (VPC) is closer to 4-6 weeks depending on network approvals. So May 10 is tight but doable if we accelerate approvals.
[04:20] Sofia: Ok, we prefer Dedicated for speed but need tight SLAs and clarity on data handling. Pricing for a 3-month pilot — what numbers are we looking at?
[04:33] Maya Chen: For a pilot we usually do a discounted committed capacity — I'll put together a 3-month pilot package with Dedicated pool sizing based on your projected throughput. We'll send the pricing sheet after this call.
[04:47] Devon: On indemnity and liability caps — our legal team typically pushes for higher caps and carveouts for gross negligence. Can you accept adjustments?
[04:58] Maya Chen: We can be reasonable; we'll review and propose language. We have some standard enterprise exceptions but open to discuss certain carveouts.
[05:12] Liam: One more security note — we need encryption of data at rest and in flight, which I assume is standard, and role-based access controls with SSO integration.
[05:23] Ravi: Yes TLS in transit and encryption at rest are standard. We support SAML2.0 SSO and RBAC in the console. For API keys we recommend short-lived tokens and audit logs.
[05:36] Maya Singh: How granular are audit logs? We need per-token cost traces and per-route latency breakdowns ideally.
[05:45] Jordan: Redwood Console provides per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. We'll include sample screenshots in the security pack.
[06:00] [00:06:00] Sofia: About subprocessors — we need the full list, and if you add any new ones we need 30-day notice.
[06:12] Maya Chen: We'll include the current subprocessor list and can commit to a 30-day notice for material changes.
[06:24] Devon: For the DPA, the data subject rights section needs to be explicit about deletion timelines. We want 7-day max for user data removal in the pilot scope.
[06:36] Jordan: For Dedicated we can commit to 7-day deletion for pilot-scoped data; on hosted we'll need to validate but can often meet 30 days. We'll add language to the DPA examples.
[06:52] Ravi: Also we'll run a quick performance benchmark during the pilot — typical tests will include concurrency stress and p99 latency measured over 24 hours. Do you have target queries per second?
[07:05] Maya Singh: We're planning for around 150 qps peak for inferencing for our routing assistant, average 40 qps.
[07:14] Ravi: Ok that's helpful; we'll size Dedicated GPU pool recommendations around that and include batching profiles to keep costs down.
[07:25] Sofia: On pricing approvals — our finance needs fixed pilot pricing for sign-off, not a ballpark.
[07:34] Maya Chen: We'll send a firm pilot quote with the recommended capacity, a discounted rate for the 3-month commit, and an optional roll-forward rate if you convert to annual reserved.
[07:47] Devon: We will likely need the MSA redline from Redwood before our counsel will sign anything. Please mark any non-negotiable clauses so we can escalate.
[07:59] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll highlight the clauses we typically hold (like export controls, and standard liability carveouts) and flag negotiable items.
[08:12] Liam: A few technical clarifications — can Redwood support private model hosting so we bring our own model behind your runtime?
[08:24] Ravi: Yes, on Private or Dedicated we support customer-provided models; there are some validation steps for compatibility, and we can run model onboarding tests.
[08:36] Maya Singh: Do you support quantized model variants? We want to optimize cost.
[08:42] Ravi: Yes we support quantized execution paths; the runtime selects kernels and quantization profiles depending on the model and sequence distribution. We'll recommend profiles for your workload.
[08:58] [00:08:58] Sofia: For the SLA table, include credits and measurement windows.
[09:06] Jordan: We'll attach our SLA appendix with credit calculations. For 99.95% uptime, credits are X% — we'll include the formal table.
[09:18] Devon: About liability insurance — can you provide certificate of insurance and evidence of cyber coverage?
[09:27] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll add our COI and cyber insurance summary to the security pack.
[09:36] Maya Singh: On observability — can we export logs to our SIEM?
[09:42] Ravi: Yes, we support log forwarding to S3 and direct integrations to Splunk/Datadog via our ingestion hooks. We'll include configuration steps.
[09:56] Sofia: I'd like to call out procurement timeline — we need signed contracts and pilot in place by May 7 to meet internal launch. Is there a path?
[10:06] Maya Chen: If we get redlines this week and accept terms quickly, we can hit that. The critical path is legal review and finance PO issuance. We'll prioritize.
[10:18] [00:10:18] Devon: Quick follow-up — our counsel wants a mutual NDA and a clause on return/destruction of customer data post-termination.
[10:27] Jordan: Standard DPA covers return/destruction language; we'll make sure it's explicit for the pilot and include retention windows.
[10:37] Liam: Are there known limitations for PII processing? We process limited PII but must ensure encryption and access controls.
[10:46] Ravi: We recommend tokenization at the app layer but the platform supports access controls and audit logging. For higher assurance, private deployment with customer KMS is best.
[10:59] Maya Chen: Ok, I'll summarize next steps at the end and we'll capture action items.
[11:06] [00:11:06] Sofia: One last procurement ask — any preferred vendor forms to complete? We can do our standard vendor setup but if you have vendor questionnaire templates, send them.
[11:16] Maya Chen: We'll send our vendor info pack and a completed SSF that usually speeds up vendor onboarding.
[11:24] Devon: For the DPA, do you accept a data protection addendum with our specific wording?
[11:33] Maya Chen: We accept customer redlines and we'll try to accommodate reasonable language; we'll flag anything that needs legal escalation.
[11:43] Ravi: On technical benchmarks, we'll propose a 48-hour soak test with p50/p95/p99 reporting and cost-per-token estimates, and we'll run a joint runbook.
[11:55] Maya Singh: Sounds good. We'll share example prompts and sequences ahead of the test.
[12:03] [00:12:03] Jordan: I'll schedule the technical kick-off once we have an agreed pilot scope.
[12:10] Sofia: Moving to any blockers — none from my side other than legal approvals and pricing finalization.
[12:18] Devon: Same. We need to review redlines.
[12:23] Maya Chen: Great — we'll aim to get the MSA/DPA to you by Tuesday. Ravi will share the benchmark plan by Thursday. Jordan will send onboarding dates.
[12:35] [00:12:35] Maya Chen (AE): Recap — Redwood to send redlined MSA & DPA + SOC2 and COI, pilot pricing for 3 months with Dedicated sizing, benchmark/runbook, and onboarding timeline. Tidewater to review redlines and provide feedback by 2026-04-30.
[12:52] Sofia: That works. Thanks everyone.
[12:58] Devon: Thanks.
[13:01] Liam: Thanks all.
[13:05] [00:13:05] Maya Chen: Ok we'll follow up in email with attachments and proposed dates. Thanks, meeting adjourned.
